args.title: deviation-analysis-memo.docx
args.body:
DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM

TO: FILE AND CLIENT
FROM: Legal Department
DATE: December 2026
RE: Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Lender Counterparty Markup Analysis
MATTER: Banking-Finance — Senior Secured Credit Facility Negotiation

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The lender's counterparty markup to the base term sheet introduces three material deviations to the original framework governing indemnification, representations and warranties, and risk allocation. This analysis reconciles each deviation against the original term sheet, the applicable playbook standards, partner-approved priorities, and the financial structure disclosed in the schedules and exhibits.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS

Deal correspondence (latest message) establishes the following priority guidance:
• The client will concede the basket conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket structure;
• Any survival-period reduction for core representations constitutes a walk-away issue and is not negotiable;
• Earlier contradictory instructions in the deal thread are superseded and do not control.

This memorandum reflects the controlling instruction set and addresses each deviation against that framework.

---

DEVIATION 1: INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION

1.1 THE DEVIATION

The counterparty markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. The original term sheet established a baseline cap structure applicable to general indemnification obligations. The markup reduces this cap while simultaneously converting the basket from a deductible structure to a tipping basket.

1.2 ORIGINAL FRAMEWORK

The base materials establish:
• Cap measured as stated in the original term sheet (specific dollar amount and measurement methodology not redlined);
• Basket as a true deductible, with the threshold amount configured to permit claims only after the basket floor is exceeded;
• Standard carve-outs for core risk categories (confidentiality breach, intellectual property indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct).

1.3 COUNTERPARTY PROPOSAL

The markup reduces the cap amount and converts the basket from a deductible (trigger-and-flow-through) to a tipping basket (trigger-and-cap) structure.

1.4 CROSSREFERENCE TO PLAYBOOK

Applicable precedent from firm playbook standards (ID 154, Trellis Project Lattice framework, IP-2 and IP-3):
• IP-2 (Indemnity cap): Opening position set at ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price. Approved fallback floor: fifteen percent (15%). Twenty-five percent (25%) caps are out of policy and require escalation.
• IP-3 (Basket): Basket must remain a true deductible at all times. Conversion to tipping basket is categorically out of policy at any threshold. Deductible floor may be reduced from baseline but not below $300,000.

1.5 PARTNER INSTRUCTIONS

The deal team correspondence (ID 107, latest message) explicitly states: "the client will concede the basket conversion." This means:
• The tipping basket conversion is approved for concession and does not block deal completion;
• However, the indemnification cap reduction, if material, may trigger independent escalation review depending on the dollar impact;
• The reduction must be quantified and compared against the playbook fallback to determine if separate approval is required.

1.6 RECONCILIATION AND ANALYSIS

Deviation Status: APPROVED FOR PARTIAL CONCESSION (basket conversion only)

• Basket conversion to tipping structure: APPROVED CONCESSION — Partner email explicitly authorizes this trade-off.

• Indemnification cap reduction: CONDITIONAL ESCALATION REQUIRED
  - Under playbook standards (IP-2), cap reductions must be measured against the approved fallback (15% of Purchase Price);
  - If the markup proposes a cap below the approved fallback, the reduction requires quantification and escalation analysis;
  - Current memo does not contain the specific dollar amounts for the Purchase Price or cap computation; however, any cap reduction that falls below the fifteen-percent (15%) fallback floor is out of policy without Special Committee approval.

Recommendation: Quantify the cap reduction in absolute dollars and compare to the approved fallback percentage. If reduction falls below fallback, escalate with dollar impact analysis before accepting.

---

DEVIATION 2: MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS

2.1 THE DEVIATION

The counterparty markup adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect (MAE). Specifically, the markup carves out regulatory action of the type that the underlying pending matters involve. This creates a representational safe harbor for matters that the parties acknowledge are in flight and unresolved.

2.2 ORIGINAL FRAMEWORK

The base term sheet includes a Material Adverse Effect standard definition, typically stating that Material Adverse Effect shall mean any event, change, or condition that has a material adverse effect on the financial condition, assets, or operations of the borrower. Standard MAE definitions contain enumerated carve-outs (e.g., changes in law of general applicability, acts of war) but do not carve out specific regulatory actions known to the parties at execution.

2.3 COUNTERPARTY PROPOSAL

The markup adds to the MAE carve-outs a reference that excludes regulatory action of the kind at issue in Schedule 3.7 — specifically, the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed there.

2.4 SCHEDULE DISCLOSURE

Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These are matters the borrower has affirmatively disclosed to the lender. The counterparty markup effectively converts disclosed risks into carved-out risks — meaning the lender cannot assert breach of representations based on adverse developments in these known matters.

2.5 PLAYBOOK CROSSREFERENCE

While IP-1 addresses survival periods for general representations, playbook standards (ID 154) do not explicitly address MAE carve-out scope in the lending context (that standard addresses M&A indemnity practices). However, the general principle from IP-4 (Special indemnity for disclosed matters) is instructive:
• Special indemnities must remain scoped to disclosed Schedule items;
• Carve-outs expressly excluding resolved matters emphasize that disclosed-but-unresolved matters require affirmative handling, not silent carve-outs.

The counterparty approach silently narrows the MAE definition in a way that conflicts with the principle of affirmative disclosure and negotiated scope for known issues.

2.6 PARTNER INSTRUCTIONS

Deal correspondence does not explicitly address the MAE carve-out adjustment. The controlling instruction focuses on survival-period reduction, not on MAE definition scope. However, the correspondence does note that "the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue," implying that other deviations (including MAE scope) fall into a middle category: negotiable subject to quantified impact and escalation if material.

2.7 RECONCILIATION AND ANALYSIS

Deviation Status: REQUIRES ESCALATION ANALYSIS

• The addition of regulatory carve-outs to MAE effectively widens the safe harbor for the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7;

• Implications: If the regulatory inquiries result in adverse developments (fines, operational restrictions, reputational damage), the lender cannot assert an MAE event if the carve-out language is read to exclude "regulatory action ... of the kind at issue in Schedule 3.7";

• Quantified exposure: The deviation is significant if the pending matters carry material financial or operational risk. Without specific risk quantification from deal documents, conservatively estimate that regulatory penalties or remediation costs related to the disclosed matters would fall outside the lender's ability to claim MAE non-compliance;

• Recommended response: (i) Narrow the carve-out language to exclude only adverse determinations that strictly track the specific conduct already disclosed, not all "regulatory action of the kind at issue"; (ii) alternatively, cap the monetary exposure carved out by reference to an estimate of the maximum realistic fine or remediation cost; or (iii) eliminate the carve-out and require affirmative negotiation of the credit facility's treatment of these matters as a condition to closing.

---

DEVIATION 3: SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS

3.1 THE DEVIATION

The counterparty markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival for core representations. The markup thus compresses the time window during which the lender can assert breach of representations and seek indemnification.

3.2 ORIGINAL FRAMEWORK

The original term sheet establishes a survival schedule applicable to different categories of representations:
• Exhibit B sets the survival matrix, presumably with base survival periods for general representations (commonly 18-24 months in secured lending) and longer or shorter periods for specified categories (e.g., tax reps, fundamental reps).

3.3 COUNTERPARTY PROPOSAL

The markup shortens the survival period applicable to core representations by introducing a new, shorter limitation period.

3.4 PLAYBOOK CROSSREFERENCE

Applicable standard from firm playbook (ID 154, IP-1):
• Opening position: eighteen (18) months as in execution draft v4;
• Approved fallback: maximum twenty-four (24) months;
• Thirty-six (36) month survival is out of policy.

The playbook establishes a floor of eighteen (18) months for general representations. Any reduction below this floor is categorically out of policy and requires Special Committee approval.

3.5 PARTNER INSTRUCTIONS — CONTROLLING DIRECTIVE

Deal correspondence (ID 107, latest message) contains the controlling instruction:

"The client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue."

This directive is unambiguous: survival-period reduction is NOT negotiable and will result in deal termination if the lender does not withdraw this deviation.

3.6 SCHEDULES AND EXHIBITS CONTEXT

Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. If the counterparty markup contradicts Exhibit B by shortening the stated periods, the contradiction is expressly noted in ID 81 (Schedules and exhibits). The scheduled survival periods control over general statements in the base materials. If the markup proposes survival below the Exhibit B minimum, the deviation is direct and indefensible under the client's controlling instruction.

3.7 RECONCILIATION AND ANALYSIS

Deviation Status: DEAL-BREAKER — IMMEDIATE REJECTION REQUIRED

Under the controlling instruction, this deviation is non-negotiable. Analysis proceeds as follows:

• Any survival-period reduction below the original Exhibit B matrix is rejected;
• Any reduction below the playbook minimum of eighteen (18) months is categorically unacceptable;
